per_object_cap.stated: If you price your product at any number greater than $0.99, the largest single file that you can upload to a product is 20 GB in size.
per_object_cap.notes: 20 GB per file applies to a product priced above $0.99; a free product is limited to 250 MB. The help article words the threshold both as greater than $0.99 and as higher than $1.

retention.stated: The terms state that Gumroad has no obligation to store any of Your Content that you Make Available on the Services.
retention.notes: Unpublishing a product does not delete the product or its data. Deleting a product is permanent and cannot be undone.

interface_detail: Web + documented REST API (products, product_files); the codebase is open source (antiwork/gumroad), so limits are inspectable.
tooling: REST API with access token; the repo exposes /attachments/... presigned paths via SignedUrlHelper.
chaining: Pricing a product above $0.99 raises the largest single file to 20 GB, and a product can hold as many files as you want. A product priced at $0 is limited to 250 MB of files in total.

limits_note: Per-object-cap 20 GB (products >$0.99) / 250 MB cumulative (priced $0). 'Download all' button only appears under 500 MB total content, but a single ZIP sidesteps that. Repo shows MAX_EPUB_READER_ARCHIVE_SIZE = 32 MB and thumbnail cap 5 MB. Those are feature caps, not the product-file cap.

identity_cost.detail: an email address and a password, or a Google or X sign-in, on the signup form. No card and no phone number appear on that form, and uploading files needs no payout profile; withdrawing sales runs a Stripe identity check that asks for a date of birth, phone number and possibly a government ID.

reliability_note: Purchases require a payment method on the seller side to withdraw, but uploading does not. Download URLs are presigned CloudFront/S3 and short-lived, so there is no stable hot-link. Archive/delivery tier only.

extras.agent_focus: Print-on-demand, media and fulfilment platforms that host your uploads permanently and serve them cheaply. The question for every candidate was NOT 'can I upload' (all of them accept uploads) but: does the platform serve my ORIGINAL bytes back, unsigned, indefinitely, from a CDN I can hot-link? POD image hosts (Redbubble/Printful/Printify/Society6/Threadless/Zazzle/Etsy) all re-encode, cap at 20-300 MB and gate the write behind account setup — they are inverted (tiny ingress, no egress). The value in this niche is the DIGITAL-PRODUCT fulfilment layer and the 3D-model repositories, which are the two places where arbitrary file types survive ingest at GB scale.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
